proposed.explanation: At the cutoff price of 141.95 EGP per share, your 300 shares of ETEL are worth 42,585.00 EGP, which together with 20,000.00 EGP in cash gives a total portfolio value of 62,585.00 EGP (68.04% concentrated in ETEL). In FY2025 (ended 31/12/2025), ETEL generated consolidated operating revenues of 106,672,946,000 EGP. This was up 30.60% from FY2024 consolidated operating revenues of 81,677,812,000 EGP. Consolidated gross profit reached 44,839,110,000 EGP in FY2025, expanding the gross margin to 42.03%. In FY2024, consolidated gross profit was 30,492,762,000 EGP (a 37.33% gross margin). On the balance sheet as of 31/12/2025, ETEL held consolidated total assets of 225,882,527,000 EGP. Consolidated total equity as of 31/12/2025 stood at 63,687,826,000 EGP, implying total liabilities of 162,194,701,000 EGP and a liabilities-to-equity ratio of about 2.55x. However, the available evidence is not sufficient to make a responsible buy, hold, or sell decision for your child's 5-7 year university savings goal, especially given your medium risk tolerance and 68.04% concentration in a single stock. Crucial information is missing: (1) bottom-line profitability (operating expenses, financing costs, taxes, and net profit) to verify whether gross profit translates into net earnings despite the large liability base; (2) operating and free cash flows, capital expenditure requirements, and debt maturity profile; (3) the number of shares outstanding, earnings per share, and dividend history needed to judge whether the 141.95 EGP share price is fairly valued; and (4) any 2026 interim financial results between 31/12/2025 and the 2026-11-18 cutoff. No trade or portfolio change is recommended until full FY2025 statements and current 2026 interim figures are reviewed; note that this is guidance rather than a guarantee of future returns, and single-stock concentration carries substantial downside risk.
